items.title: 5.5 Equation of Lines Through the Point of Intersection of Two Lines (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book pp. 149-153: 5.5 family of lines l1 + k l2 = 0, Example 11 (a), (b), Theorems 4-6 (altitudes, right bisectors, medians concurrent) with Figures 5.5-5.7.

blocks.text: Bachon, ab ek bahut kaam ki cheez seekhte hain. Farz karein do lines ek point par milti hain aur humein aisi line chahiye jo usi point se guzre aur saath mein koi aur shart bhi poori kare (jaise kisi line ke parallel ho). Seedha tareeqa yeh hai ke pehle intersection point nikalo, phir line banao. Lekin ek shortcut bhi hai jo point nikale baghair kaam kar deta hai: family of lines. Family ka matlab hai lines ka aisa khandan jis ki har line ek hi point se guzarti hai, jaise cycle ke pahiye ki saari tiliyan (spokes) beech wale dhure (hub) se guzarti hain.

Do non-parallel lines \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) lein:
\[\ell_1 : a_1x + b_1y + c_1 = 0 \quad \ldots(i)\]
aur
\[\ell_2 : a_2x + b_2y + c_2 = 0 \quad \ldots(ii)\]

Kisi non-zero real number \(k\) ke liye yeh equation dekhein:
\[a_1x + b_1y + c_1\]
\[+ k(a_2x + b_2y + c_2) = 0 \;\ldots(iii)\]
Yeh linear equation hai (is mein \(x\) aur \(y\) ki power sirf 1 hai), is liye yeh ek straight line hai. \(k\) ki har nayi value ek nayi line deti hai, is liye (iii) lines ki ek family hai.

Ab dekhte hain ke yeh saari lines ek hi point se kyun guzarti hain. Agar \((x_1, y_1)\) aisa point hai jo (i) aur (ii) dono par hai, to yahi un ka intersection point hai. Kyunke yeh dono lines par hai, is liye
\[a_1x_1 + b_1y_1 + c_1 = 0\]
aur
\[a_2x_1 + b_2y_1 + c_2 = 0\]
Ab is point ko (iii) mein rakhein: pehla bracket zero, doosra bracket bhi zero, to \(0 + k \cdot 0 = 0\). Yani \((x_1, y_1)\) (iii) par bhi hai, \(k\) kuch bhi ho.
Lehaza (iii) un lines ki family hai jo (i) aur (ii) ke intersection point se guzarti hain. \(k\) be-shumaar values le sakta hai, is liye (iii) be-shumaar lines ko zahir karti hai. Family mein se koi ek khaas line chunne ke liye ek aur shart chahiye hoti hai.

blocks.text_alt: l1 plus k times l2 equals zero

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
(iii) line kyun hai? Terms ikatthe karein: \((a_1 + ka_2)x + (b_1 + kb_2)y + (c_1 + kc_2) = 0\), jo \(x\) aur \(y\) mein first degree hai. (\(x\) aur \(y\) ke coefficients dono ek saath zero nahi ho sakte, warna \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) parallel hotin.)
Faida kya hai? Intersection point nikale baghair hum required line tak pohanch jate hain; bas ek aur shart (parallel, perpendicular, kisi point se guzarna) se \(k\) maloom karna hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Chhoti si baat: \(k = 0\) se \(\ell_1\) khud milti hai, lekin \(k\) ki kisi bhi value se \(\ell_2\) nahi milti. Agar kabhi required line \(\ell_2\) hi ho to \(k\) ki equation ka koi hal nahi niklega; aisi soorat mein \(\ell_2\) ko seedha check kar lein.

Ek misaal se samjhein ke family kitni kaam ki hai. Farz karein do sarkein ek chowk par milti hain aur aap ko us chowk se guzarne wali teesri sarak banani hai jo kisi nehar ke parallel ho. Aap ke paas chowk ka naqsha nahi, sirf dono sarkon ki equations hain. Family of lines kehti hai: chowk dhoondne ki zaroorat nahi; dono equations ko jor kar ek 'k' wali equation bana lo, aur nehar ke parallel hone ki shart se k nikal lo. Jo line milegi woh khud ba khud chowk se guzregi.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(x - y = 0\) aur \(x + y - 2 = 0\) ki family \(x - y + k(x + y - 2) = 0\) hai. \(k = 1\) rakhein to \(2x - 2 = 0\), yani \(x = 1\); \(k = -1\) rakhein to \(-2y + 2 = 0\), yani \(y = 1\). Dono lines \((1, 1)\) se guzarti hain, jo bilkul pehli do lines ka meeting point hai. Ab aap \(k = 2\) rakh kar khud dekhiye ke line \((1, 1)\) se guzarti hai ya nahi.

Ab Example 11. Sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke sawal kya maang raha hai: pehle poori family likhni hai, phir us family mein se do khaas members chunne hain: ek jo di hui slope ke parallel ho, aur ek jo di hui line par perpendicular ho.

blocks.title: Example 11
blocks.problem:
Find the family of lines through the point of intersection of the lines \(2x - 3y - 14 = 0\) and \(2x + y - 10 = 0\). Find the member of the family which is:
(a) parallel to the line with slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\)
(b) perpendicular to the line \(2x - 3y + 2 = 0\)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2x - 3y - 14 = 0\) ...(i) aur \(2x + y - 10 = 0\) ...(ii).
Maloom karna: in ke intersection point se guzarne wali lines ki family, aur us ke members (a) slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\) wali line ke parallel, (b) \(2x - 3y + 2 = 0\) par perpendicular.
Tareeqa: family \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) likhenge, us ki slope \(k\) mein nikalenge, phir slope ki shart (parallel ke liye \(m_1 = m_2\), perpendicular ke liye \(m_1m_2 = -1\)) se \(k\) maloom karenge. Is tarah intersection point nikalne ki zaroorat hi nahi.

Family likhein
(i) aur (ii) ke intersection point se guzarne wali lines ki family:
\[2x - 3y - 14 + k(2x + y - 10) = 0\]
\[(2 + 2k)x + (k - 3)y\]
\[+ (-14 - 10k) = 0 \;\ldots(iii)\]
Kyun: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) har \(k\) ke liye meeting point se guzarti hai. \(x\) wale terms, \(y\) wale terms aur constants ko alag alag ikattha kiya to general form ban gayi.
Dhyan dein: \(-10\) ko bhi \(k\) se multiply karna hai, yani \(-10k\); yeh aksar bhool jata hai.

Family ki slope
(iii) ki slope:
\[m = -\dfrac{2 + 2k}{k - 3}\]
Kyun: \(ax + by + c = 0\) ki slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\) hoti hai; yahan \(a = 2 + 2k\) aur \(b = k - 3\). Yeh family ki har line ki slope hai, bas \(k\) badalta rahta hai.

(a) Parallel: slopes barabar rakhein
Agar (iii) slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\) wali line ke parallel hai to
\[-\dfrac{2 + 2k}{k - 3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[4 + 4k = k - 3\]
\[3k = -7\]
\[k = -\dfrac{7}{3}\]
Kyun: parallel lines ki slopes barabar hoti hain. \(\frac{2 + 2k}{k - 3} = \frac{1}{2}\) ko cross-multiply karein to \(2(2 + 2k) = k - 3\) milta hai.

(a) \(k = -\frac{7}{3}\) ko (iii) mein rakhein
\[\left(2 + 2\left(-\tfrac{7}{3}\right)\right)x + \left(-\tfrac{7}{3} - 3\right)y\]
\[+ \left(-14 - 10\left(-\tfrac{7}{3}\right)\right) = 0\]
\[\left(\tfrac{6 - 14}{3}\right)x + \left(\tfrac{-7 - 9}{3}\right)y + \left(\tfrac{-42 + 70}{3}\right) = 0\]
\[-\tfrac{8}{3}x - \tfrac{16}{3}y + \tfrac{28}{3} = 0\]
\[-8x - 16y + 28 = 0\]
\[2x + 4y - 7 = 0\]
Kyun: har coefficient mein value rakhi, har bracket ko denominator 3 par simplify kiya, 3 se multiply kiya aur phir \(-4\) se divide kar ke sab se saada shakal banai. Yahi family ka required member hai.

(b) Perpendicular: slopes ka product \(-1\)
\(2x - 3y + 2 = 0\) ...(iv) ki slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) hai. (iii) is par perpendicular hai, is liye
\[-\dfrac{2 + 2k}{k - 3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = -1\]
\[4 + 4k = 3k - 9\]
\[k = -13\]
Kyun: perpendicular lines ke liye \(m_1m_2 = -1\). Left side \(-\frac{2(2 + 2k)}{3(k - 3)} = -1\) banta hai, yani \(2(2 + 2k) = 3(k - 3)\).

Tasdeeq:
Lines (i) aur (ii) \(\left(\frac{11}{2}, -1\right)\) par milti hain ((i) mein se (ii) minus karein: \(-4y = 4\)).
\[2\left(\tfrac{11}{2}\right) + 4(-1) - 7 = 0\]
\[6\left(\tfrac{11}{2}\right) + 4(-1) - 29 = 0\]
Slopes: \(2x + 4y - 7 = 0\) ki slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\); \(6x + 4y - 29 = 0\) ki slope \(-\frac{3}{2}\), aur \(-\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = -1\). Dono jawab sahi hain.

blocks.text: Is misaal ka khulasa: humne intersection point \(\left(\frac{11}{2}, -1\right)\) nikala hi nahi, phir bhi dono lines mil gayin. Family ne point ka kaam khud sambhal liya, aur humein sirf slope ki shart se \(k\) dhoondna para. Agar sawal kehta ke line kisi diye hue point se guzre, to hum us point ko (iii) mein rakh kar \(k\) nikalte. Yani tareeqa hamesha ek hai: family likho, ek shart lagao, \(k\) nikalo, wapas rakho.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Neeche Theorems 4, 5 aur 6 mein ek hi tarkeeb teen dafa istemal hoti hai: triangle ki teen khaas lines ko general form mein likho, Theorem 3 lagao, aur doosri aur teesri row ko pehli row mein jama karo. Pehli row poori zero ho jati hai, determinant zero ho jata hai, aur lines concurrent saabit ho jati hain. Yeh tarkeeb ek dafa samajh li to teeno theorems aasaan ho jayenge.

Ab hum triangle ke teen mash-hoor nataij (results) parhenge. Class 9 aur 10 ki geometry mein aap ne shayad yeh baat compass aur ruler se dekhi ho ke teeno medians ek point par milte hain. Wahan hum figure bana kar dekhte the; yahan hum coordinates aur determinant ki madad se isay har triangle ke liye saabit karenge. Yahi analytical geometry ki taqat hai: shakal ki baat ko algebra mein badal kar pakka saboot dena. Har theorem mein pehle ek line ki equation nikalenge, baqi do 'by symmetry' likhenge, aur phir Theorem 3 lagayenge.
Theorem 4
Kisi bhi triangle ke altitudes concurrent hote hain, yani teeno altitudes ek hi point se guzarte hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par triangle A(x1, y1) upar, B(x2, y2) neeche baayen, C(x3, y3) neeche daayen, magenta sides. Altitudes AD, BE aur CF cyan rang mein, paon par right angle ke nishan; teeno andar ek point O par milti hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.5: The altitudes AD, BE and CF of triangle ABC meet at O (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.5)

blocks.text:
Proof: Sab se pehle triangle ke vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) le lete hain, jaisa figure mein hai. Altitude \(AD\) vertex \(A\) se guzarta hai aur side \(BC\) par perpendicular hai. Is liye pehle \(BC\) ki slope chahiye: \(\overline{BC}\) ki slope \(= \frac{y_2 - y_3}{x_2 - x_3}\). Perpendicular lines ki slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai, is liye altitude \(AD\) ki slope \(= -\frac{x_2 - x_3}{y_2 - y_3}\) (ulta karo aur sign badlo). Ab point-slope form lagate hain, kyunke humare paas ek point \(A\) aur slope dono hain:
\[y - y_1 = -\dfrac{x_2 - x_3}{y_2 - y_3}(x - x_1)\]
Dono taraf \((y_2 - y_3)\) se multiply kar ke sab terms ek taraf le jayen to:
\[x(x_2 - x_3) + y(y_2 - y_3)\]
\[- x_1(x_2 - x_3) - y_1(y_2 - y_3) = 0 \;\ldots(i)\]

Baqi do altitudes \(BE\) aur \(CF\) ki equations hum dobara nahi nikalte; 'by symmetry' (ussi naqsh par) labels badal kar likh lete hain:
\[x(x_3 - x_1) + y(y_3 - y_1)\]
\[- x_2(x_3 - x_1) - y_2(y_3 - y_1) = 0 \;\ldots(ii)\]
aur
\[x(x_1 - x_2) + y(y_1 - y_2)\]
\[- x_3(x_1 - x_2) - y_3(y_1 - y_2) = 0 \;\ldots(iii)\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
'By symmetry' ka matlab: (i) mein har label ko triangle ke gird ek qadam aage kar do, \(1 \to 2\), \(2 \to 3\), \(3 \to 1\) (A se B, B se C, C se A). Is tarah \(B\) se altitude \(CA\) par perpendicular hai aur \((x_2, y_2)\) se guzarta hai, aur wohi equation (ii) ban jati hai.
Ek aur khoobsurat baat: (i) asal mein \((x - x_1)(x_2 - x_3) + (y - y_1)(y_2 - y_3) = 0\) hai. Is shakal mein yeh tab bhi sahi hai jab \(BC\) horizontal ya vertical ho (jahan slope wali fraction ka denominator zero ho jata), is liye proof har triangle par lagta hai.

Ab Theorem 3 lagate hain: lines (i), (ii), (iii) tab aur sirf tab concurrent hain jab un ke coefficients ka determinant zero ho:
\[\begin{vmatrix} x_2 - x_3 & y_2 - y_3 & p_1 \\ x_3 - x_1 & y_3 - y_1 & p_2 \\ x_1 - x_2 & y_1 - y_2 & p_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
jahan \(p_1 = -x_1(x_2 - x_3) - y_1(y_2 - y_3)\), \(p_2 = -x_2(x_3 - x_1) - y_2(y_3 - y_1)\) aur \(p_3 = -x_3(x_1 - x_2) - y_3(y_1 - y_2)\) teeno lines ke constant terms hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yeh determinant aakhir mein '\(= 0\)' ke baghair chhapti hai. Theorem 3 ki shart yeh hai ke determinant zero ke barabar ho, is liye yahan '\(= 0\)' hona chahiye (kitab ki agli line mein \(= 0\) maujood hai).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Phone ki screen par poora likhna mushkil hai, is liye teesre column ki lambi entries ko humne \(p_1\), \(p_2\), \(p_3\) ka naam diya hai; kitab inhein poora likhti hai. Yeh bas teeno lines ke constant terms \(c\) hain, bilkul Theorem 3 ki tarah.

Ab ek chalaki: determinant ki doosri aur teesri row ko pehli row mein jama kar dein (is se determinant ki value nahi badalti):
\[\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ x_3 - x_1 & y_3 - y_1 & p_2 \\ x_1 - x_2 & y_1 - y_2 & p_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Jis determinant ki ek poori row zero ho, us ki value zero hoti hai. Lehaza triangle ke altitudes concurrent hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Pehli row zero kyun hui? Column 1: \((x_2 - x_3) + (x_3 - x_1) + (x_1 - x_2) = 0\), har term ek dafa plus aur ek dafa minus aata hai. Column 2 mein yahi kaam \(y\) ke saath. Column 3: \(p_1 + p_2 + p_3 = 0\), kyunke \(x_1x_2\) jaisa har product ek dafa \(+\) aur ek dafa \(-\) ke saath aata hai. Altitudes kabhi parallel nahi hote (woh aisi sides par perpendicular hain jo khud parallel nahi), is liye Theorem 3 lagta hai. Altitudes ke common point \(O\) ko orthocentre kehte hain (yeh naam humari taraf se hai, kitab yahan nahi likhti).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya orthocentre hamesha triangle ke andar hota hai? Socho: acute triangle (sab angles 90 se kam) mein andar, right-angled triangle mein bilkul right angle wale vertex par, aur obtuse triangle mein bahar. Lekin har haal mein teeno altitudes (ya un ko lamba karne se bani lines) ek hi point par milti hain; proof mein humne kahin yeh farz nahi kiya ke point andar hai.

Theorem 4 ka khulasa: humne koi khaas triangle nahi liya tha, balke bilkul aam vertices liye the. Is liye yeh saboot duniya ke har triangle par lagu hota hai. Ab isi andaz mein right bisectors ki baari hai. Farq sirf itna hai ke right bisector vertex se nahi, balke side ke mid-point se guzarta hai.
Theorem 5
Kisi bhi triangle ki sides ke right bisectors (perpendicular bisectors, yani woh lines jo side ke mid-point se guzrein aur us par perpendicular hon) concurrent hote hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par triangle A(x1, y1), B(x2, y2), C(x3, y3), magenta sides. Mid-points D, E, F par un ke coordinates (do coordinates ka aadha jor) likhe hain; har mid-point se perpendicular segment (right angle ke nishan ke saath) andar jata hai aur DO, EO, FO ek point O par milte hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.6: The right bisectors of the sides of triangle ABC meet at O (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.6)

blocks.text:
Proof: Vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) lete hain. Right bisector ke liye do cheezein chahiye: ek point (side ka mid-point) aur ek slope (side par perpendicular). \(BC\) ka mid-point \(D\) yeh hai: \(\left(\frac{x_2 + x_3}{2}, \frac{y_2 + y_3}{2}\right)\). \(\overline{BC}\) ki slope \(\frac{y_2 - y_3}{x_2 - x_3}\) hai, is liye right bisector \(DO\) ki slope \(-\frac{x_2 - x_3}{y_2 - y_3}\) hai. Point-slope form se \(DO\) ki equation:
\[y - \dfrac{y_2 + y_3}{2}\]
\[= -\dfrac{x_2 - x_3}{y_2 - y_3}\left(x - \dfrac{x_2 + x_3}{2}\right)\]
ya, sab kuch ek taraf le ja kar,
\[x(x_2 - x_3) + y(y_2 - y_3)\]
\[- \tfrac{1}{2}(y_2^2 - y_3^2) - \tfrac{1}{2}(x_2^2 - x_3^2) = 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab is pehli equation par (i) ka number nahi likhti, lekin aage isi ko (i) kehti hai. Yeh shakal kaise bani? Dono taraf \(y_2 - y_3\) se multiply karein, sab terms ek taraf layein, aur difference of squares istemal karein: \(\left(y - \frac{y_2 + y_3}{2}\right)(y_2 - y_3) = y(y_2 - y_3) - \frac{1}{2}(y_2^2 - y_3^2)\). \(x\) wala hissa bhi bilkul isi tarah banta hai.

By symmetry (labels ek qadam aage kar ke) baqi do right bisectors \(EO\) aur \(FO\) ki equations:
\[x(x_3 - x_1) + y(y_3 - y_1)\]
\[- \tfrac{1}{2}(y_3^2 - y_1^2) - \tfrac{1}{2}(x_3^2 - x_1^2) = 0 \;\ldots(ii)\]
aur
\[x(x_1 - x_2) + y(y_1 - y_2)\]
\[- \tfrac{1}{2}(y_1^2 - y_2^2) - \tfrac{1}{2}(x_1^2 - x_2^2) = 0 \;\ldots(iii)\]

Theorem 3 ke mutabiq lines (i), (ii), (iii) tab aur sirf tab concurrent hongi jab
\[\begin{vmatrix} x_2 - x_3 & y_2 - y_3 & q_1 \\ x_3 - x_1 & y_3 - y_1 & q_2 \\ x_1 - x_2 & y_1 - y_2 & q_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
jahan \(q_1 = -\frac{1}{2}(y_2^2 - y_3^2) - \frac{1}{2}(x_2^2 - x_3^2)\), \(q_2 = -\frac{1}{2}(y_3^2 - y_1^2) - \frac{1}{2}(x_3^2 - x_1^2)\) aur \(q_3 = -\frac{1}{2}(y_1^2 - y_2^2) - \frac{1}{2}(x_1^2 - x_2^2)\) constant terms hain (kitab inhein poora likhti hai).

Wohi chalaki dobara: doosri aur teesri row pehli row mein jama karein:
\[\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ x_3 - x_1 & y_3 - y_1 & q_2 \\ x_1 - x_2 & y_1 - y_2 & q_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Pehli row zero, to determinant zero. Lehaza triangle ke right bisectors concurrent hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan bhi har column ka jama zero hai: column 3 mein \(y_2^2 - y_3^2 + y_3^2 - y_1^2 + y_1^2 - y_2^2 = 0\), aur \(x^2\) wale terms bhi isi tarah cancel hote hain. Common point \(O\) teeno vertices \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) se barabar faasle par hai (right bisector ka har point side ke dono siron se barabar door hota hai), is liye yeh us circle ka centre hai jo teeno vertices se guzarta hai. Ise circumcentre kehte hain (yeh naam humari taraf se).

Right bisectors ka faida rozmarra zindagi mein bhi hai. Farz karein teen gaon \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) hain aur hukoomat aisa tube well lagana chahti hai jo teeno se barabar faasle par ho. Jawab: circumcentre, yani teeno right bisectors ka meeting point. Theorem 5 guarantee deta hai ke aisa ek point hamesha maujood hai, chahe gaon kahin bhi hon (bas ek seedhi line mein na hon).

Ab aakhri theorem. Is mein slope ki zaroorat nahi, kyunke median kisi side par perpendicular nahi hota. Median ke paas do pakke points hote hain: ek vertex aur samne wali side ka mid-point. Jab do points maloom hon to two-point form sab se aasaan rasta hai. Baqi kaam pehle do theorems jaisa hi hai, is liye ghabrayen nahi; lambi expressions dekh kar dar lagta hai magar har qadam wohi purana hai.
Theorem 6
Triangle ke medians concurrent hote hain. Median woh line hai jo vertex ko samne wali side ke mid-point se milati hai.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par triangle A(x1, y1) upar, B(x2, y2) aur C(x3, y3) neeche, magenta sides. Mid-points D, E, F un ke coordinates ke saath; medians AD, BE aur CF cyan rang mein ek point O par milte hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.7: The medians AD, BE and CF of triangle ABC meet at O (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.7)

blocks.text:
Proof: Vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\). Median \(AD\) do points se guzarta hai: vertex \(A\) aur \(BC\) ka mid-point \(D\left(\frac{x_2 + x_3}{2}, \frac{y_2 + y_3}{2}\right)\). Jab do points maloom hon to two-point form sab se seedha hai:
\[\dfrac{y - y_1}{\frac{y_2 + y_3}{2} - y_1} = \dfrac{x - x_1}{\frac{x_2 + x_3}{2} - x_1}\]
Cross-multiply kar ke sab terms ek taraf layein to:
\[x(y_2 + y_3 - 2y_1)\]
\[+ y(2x_1 - x_2 - x_3)\]
\[- x_1(y_2 + y_3 - 2y_1)\]
\[+ y_1(x_2 + x_3 - 2x_1) = 0 \;\ldots(i)\]

Theorem 3 se lines (i), (ii), (iii) tab aur sirf tab concurrent hongi jab
\[\begin{vmatrix} y_2 + y_3 - 2y_1 & 2x_1 - x_2 - x_3 & r_1 \\ y_3 + y_1 - 2y_2 & 2x_2 - x_3 - x_1 & r_2 \\ y_1 + y_2 - 2y_3 & 2x_3 - x_1 - x_2 & r_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
jahan \(r_1\), \(r_2\), \(r_3\) teeno lines ke constant terms hain: \(r_1 = -x_1(y_2 + y_3 - 2y_1) + y_1(x_2 + x_3 - 2x_1)\), aur \(r_2\), \(r_3\) isi tarah.

Phir wohi qadam: doosri aur teesri row pehli mein jama karein:
\[\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ y_3 + y_1 - 2y_2 & 2x_2 - x_3 - x_1 & r_2 \\ y_1 + y_2 - 2y_3 & 2x_3 - x_1 - x_2 & r_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Lehaza triangle ke medians concurrent hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Two-point form se (i) tak: dono taraf ke denominators ko 2 se multiply karein aur cross-multiply karein: \((y - y_1)(x_2 + x_3 - 2x_1) = (x - x_1)(y_2 + y_3 - 2y_1)\), phir sab ek taraf.
Medians ke common point ko centroid kehte hain: \(\left(\frac{x_1 + x_2 + x_3}{3}, \frac{y_1 + y_2 + y_3}{3}\right)\) (yeh humari taraf se izafa hai; aap (i) mein rakh kar check kar sakte hain). Centroid triangle ka 'balance point' hai: gatte ka triangle kaat kar is point par ungli rakhein to woh santulan mein rahega.

Teeno theorems ko ek saath dekhein: altitudes ka point orthocentre, right bisectors ka point circumcentre, aur medians ka point centroid. Teeno proofs ka dhancha bilkul ek jaisa tha: ek line ki equation, baqi do by symmetry, Theorem 3 ka determinant, aur rows jama kar ke zero row. Exam mein agar in mein se koi bhi theorem aaye to yahi chaar qadam likhiye; sirf pehli equation badalti hai: altitude ke liye vertex aur perpendicular slope, right bisector ke liye mid-point aur perpendicular slope, median ke liye vertex aur mid-point.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Triangle \(A(0, 0)\), \(B(6, 0)\), \(C(0, 6)\) ka centroid \(\left(\frac{0 + 6 + 0}{3}, \frac{0 + 0 + 6}{3}\right) = (2, 2)\) hai. Median \(AD\): \(D(3, 3)\), line \(y = x\), jo \((2, 2)\) se guzarti hai. Median \(BE\): \(E(0, 3)\), line \(x + 2y - 6 = 0\); \(2 + 4 - 6 = 0\). Teeno medians isi point par milte hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\ell_1 = 0\) aur \(\ell_2 = 0\) ke meeting point se guzarne wali lines: \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) (lines ki family).
2. Ek aur shart (parallel, perpendicular, kisi point se guzarna) se \(k\) aur is tarah family ka ek member maloom hota hai.
3. \((a_1 + ka_2)x + (b_1 + kb_2)y + \ldots = 0\) ki slope \(-\frac{a_1 + ka_2}{b_1 + kb_2}\) hai.
4. Har triangle ke altitudes, right bisectors aur medians concurrent hote hain (Theorems 4, 5, 6).
5. Proof ka naqsha: Theorem 3, phir rows 2 aur 3 ko row 1 mein jama kar ke zero row banana.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Family ko \(\ell_1 + \ell_2 + k = 0\) ya \(k\ell_1 = \ell_2\) jaisi ghalat shakal mein likhna: sahi shakal \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) hai, jahan \(k\) doosri poori expression ko multiply karta hai.
2. \(\ell_2\) ke constant term ko \(k\) se multiply karna bhool jana (jaise \(-14 - 10k\) ki jagah \(-14 - 10\) likh dena).
3. Perpendicular ke liye \(m_1 = m_2\) ya parallel ke liye \(m_1m_2 = -1\) laga dena; ulta yaad rakhein.
4. Altitude ya right bisector ke liye side ki slope hi le lena, perpendicular slope (ulta aur sign badla hua) ki jagah.
